full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant, to the disposal of the instant Rule are that on 11-7-1977 Md. Azahar Ali Sarker, the predecessor of the petitioners as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 180 of 1977 before the then learned Munsif, First Court, Bogra praying for a decree for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of 'ka' Schedule land as well as permanent injunction in respect of Kha Schedule land on the averments, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Maharaja Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur, and the said plaintiff Md. Azahar Ali Sarker took settlement of the same on payment of appropriate salami on 7th Chaitra, 1354 BS; that the plaintiff paid rent to his landlord on regular basis; that following the acquisition of the rent receiving interest the plaintiff paid rent to the Government and remained in possession of the suit land as a direct tenant under the Government and accordingly, MRR Khatian No. 4 in respect of the suit land was correctly prepared and finally published in his name;  that the then East Pakistan Government acquired 1896 decimals of land out of 1904 decimals from Plot No. 534 under Schedule Ga to the plaint vide LA Case No. 37 of 1952 for the purpose of rehabilitating landless persons and the plaintiff got compensation for the said land; that on 31-12-1952 the government requisitioned the lands of the suit Plot Nos. 1265 and 1267 and that of the non-suited Plot No. 1122 and thereafter on 20-10-1958 the same were derequisitioned and the possession thereof was handed over in his favour on 23-11-1958 and since then he was in exclusive possession of the suit land; that in the first part of February, 1966 the defendant Nos. 1-15 trespassed into 1.33 acres of land of Plot No. 1265 and 28 decimals of land of Plot No. 1267 on the plea that the Rehabilitation Department of the Government allotted 0.08 acres of land to each of them and they raised construction therein; that thereafter the plaintiff enquired into the concerned office of the Government but found no trace of acquisition or requisition of the suit plots; that the plaintiff was neither served any notice nor he was given any compensation against the so-called acquisition of the suit land; that the land as described in Schedule 'ka' was neither requisitioned nor acquisitioned nor it was allotted to anybody else, but the defendant Nos. 1-15 forcibly trespassed into the them and illegally dispossessed the plaintiff there from; that on 30-11-1976, the plaintiff finally became sanguine that the suit land was never requisitioned and acquisitioned by the Government and, as such, he requested the defendants to vacate the same, but the latter on refused/failed to comply with the request of the former; that after being requested to vacate the Schedule 'ka' land, the defendant Nos. 1-15 threatened to dispossess the plaintiff from the Schedule Kha land and hence, the suit. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 2-15 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the material facts of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the Government requisitioned 2.00 acres of land from Plot Nos. 1265 and 1267 for rehabilitating refugees and allotted the said land to them and they have been enjoying and possessing the same by erecting homesteads thereon; that the remaining 5.12 acres of land of the said plots remained khas and the Government allotted the same to the defendants who are cultivating different crops therein by clearing jungles therefrom; that the plaintiff has got no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and the suit being false, is liable to be dismissed.
